24 An ambulance siren emits a sound with a single frequency f.
The ambulance travels towards, passes close to, and then travels away from a stationary
observer.
Which statement describes the frequency of the sound detected by the observer as the
ambulance passes the observer?
A
equal to f and decreasing
B
equal to f and increasing
C
greater than f and constant
D
less than f and constant

hints: Notice the wording passes close to - focus on the instant of closest approach, not the long approach or recession.
Recall Doppler shift depends on the component of source velocity towards the observer, $f_o = f v/(v - v_s)$ for approach.
Think what the towards-observer component is just before, exactly at, and just after closest approach to see how $f_o$ changes through $f$.
walkthrough: Identify the geometry: the ambulance moves past a stationary observer, so well before passing it moves almost directly towards the observer and well after passing almost directly away.
State the Doppler rule: observed frequency $f_o$ is higher than $f$ when the source has a velocity component towards the observer and lower than $f$ when the component is away.
At the instant it passes closest, the ambulance velocity is perpendicular to the line joining source and observer, so the component of source speed towards the observer $v_s = 0$.
Substitute $v_s = 0$ into $f_o = f v/(v - v_s)$ to get $f_o = f v/v = f$ at that instant.
Just before passing there is still a small towards-component so $f_o > f$, and just after passing there is a small away-component so $f_o < f$, hence the detected frequency is falling through $f$.

A.explanation: At closest approach the source velocity along the line to the observer is zero, so observed frequency equals $f$, and it falls from above $f$ to below $f$ as the ambulance goes past.

B.explanation: The frequency does pass through $f$ at closest approach, but it changes from higher to lower, so it is decreasing not increasing.

C.explanation: Frequency greater than $f$ is heard only while approaching head-on, not at the instant of passing where the radial speed is zero.

D.explanation: Frequency less than $f$ is heard only while receding head-on, not at the instant of passing where the radial speed is zero.
